title: A heavier cyclotron particle
hook: Change particle mass and predict cyclotron frequency.
misconception: cyclotron frequency doubles when particle mass doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply f = abs(q)B/(2πm) to compare cyclotron frequency when particle mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a nonrelativistic particle with fixed charge in a fixed uniform magnetic field, f = abs(q)B/(2πm). When particle mass doubles, cyclotron frequency becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model f = abs(q)B/(2πm); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a nonrelativistic particle with fixed charge in a fixed uniform magnetic field, with a nonzero initial result. If particle mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on cyclotron frequency?
recall.why: Apply f = abs(q)B/(2πm) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
